title: California Enacts Over Two Dozen Key Privacy and AI Bills into Law in 2026 Legislative Session
key_facts: The California legislature passed dozens of AI and privacy bills on 31 Aug 2026, the last day of its session, starting a 30-day clock for Gov. Gavin Newsom.
Newsom signed SB 947, the 'No Robo Bosses Act of 2026', on 30 Sep 2026; it bars employers from relying solely on automated decision systems for discipline or firing.
AB 226, AB 1709 and SB 1119, child online safety bills, were signed on 10 Sep 2026.
SB 1119 adds protections for minors using companion chatbots, including independent child safety audits.
AB 883 tightens data broker deletion rules, moving the access requirement from every 45 days to every 30 days.
Wilson Sonsini's headline counts more than two dozen privacy and AI bills enacted; its page was blocked.
quote_evidence: On the day of the September 30th deadline, Governor Newsom signed SB 947 into law.
Key child online safety bills AB 226, AB 1709, and SB 1119 were all signed by Governor Newsom on September 10.
why_it_matters_hint: California is setting the practical rules for AI at work, for children online and for data brokers while Washington favours industry self-regulation.
notes: Wilson Sonsini page returned 403; WilmerHale's review of the same session read via JD Supra. The Redlands Daily Facts editorial also describes SB 947 as signed.
